# ellmos-servercommander-mcp

ellmos-servercommander-mcp is an authoritative Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for local-first server operations workflows. It exposes diagnostic and dry-run-first tools for HTTP health checks, Apache/Nginx access-log analysis, deployment manifest planning, deployment profile diagnostics, and mail configuration status.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/ellmos-ai/ellmos-servercommander-mcp
Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/ellmos-servercommander-mcp
MCP registry name: io.github.ellmos-ai/ellmos-servercommander-mcp
License: MIT
Version: 0.1.0-alpha.19 (Python 0.1.0a19)
Runtime: Node.js wrapper plus Python 3.10+ MCP server (FastMCP stdio)
Architecture: 5-Tier System (Host Layer, Node Gateway Layer, Python Core Server Layer, Operations Engines, Local Storage & Audit Sink)
Navigation: 15-point standardized quick navigation with 100% bilingual parity across README.md and README_de.md

## Audience & Target Personas

- Autonomous AI Agent Engineers & Tooling Architects: MCP tool-calling agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Antigravity) requiring safe server diagnostics.
- DevOps & Site Reliability Engineers (SREs): Preflight deployment verification with recursive SHA-256 tree manifests.
- Security-Conscious System Administrators: Forensic access log analysis, unprivileged RunAsInvoker execution, and strict secret isolation.
- Solo Developers & Maintainers: Fast, zero-configuration HTTP endpoint health probing directly from IDE.

## Current Tools

- `sc_health_check`: checks HTTP endpoints and reports status code plus latency; non-blocking worker threads.
- `sc_logs_analyze`: analyzes Apache/Nginx access logs from inline text or a local file path; supports optional JSON report persistence.
- `sc_deploy`: builds a safe dry-run deployment plan with a local SHA256 manifest and profile diagnostics; tracks skipped symlinks; can optionally persist the dry-run plan in local SQLite history.
- `sc_deploy_status`: shows configured deployment profiles and recent dry-run deployment history from local SQLite.
- `sc_mail_list`, `sc_mail_read`, `sc_mail_send`, `sc_mail_search`: mail configuration diagnostics without IMAP/SMTP execution by default.

## Governance & Runtime Invariants

- INV-LOCAL-01: 100% Local-First & Zero-Egress (Local diagnostic and dry-run execution; zero unverified outbound telemetry)
- INV-DRY-02: Fail-Safe Deployment Staging (Default dry_run=True; manifest calculation & SHA-256 tree hashing before target execution)
- INV-LOG-03: Sanitized Access-Log Analysis (Read-only parse; regex token extraction; optional structured JSON output without credential leaks)
- INV-PROBE-04: Non-Blocking Resilient Health Probes (Worker thread HTTP GET with strict timeouts; resilient error handling without aborting batches)
- INV-MAIL-05: Dry-Run Mail Configuration Status (Readiness checks report gaps without sending emails; protocol verification only)
- INV-PRIV-06: Non-Elevation / RunAsInvoker (Unprivileged user mode; zero sudo/root/UAC requirements)
- INV-SEC-07: Safe Process & Working Directory Isolation (PYTHONSAFEPATH=1; hardened launcher against rogue working directory packages)
- INV-I18N-08: Native Multi-Language i18n Engine (6 locales: en, de, es, zh, ja, ru with automated English fallback)
- INV-SYNC-09: Cloud-Sync & Multi-Agent Lock Hardening (.gitignore hardened against sync conflicts and multi-agent locks)
- INV-SLA-10: 48-Hour Response & 5-Day Triage SLA (Direct security response via security@ellmos.ai and security@open-bricks.org)

## Disambiguation

This is not the GitHub MCP server, not a generic arbitrary shell-command MCP server, not a cloud-hosted control panel, and not a production SFTP/IMAP executor yet. The alpha release is intentionally diagnostic, dry-run-first, local-first, and safe by default.
